answer: In a land-data exchange, a buyer requests separate reports on a meadow and a nearby hollow. Before bidding, each agent commits to raw sensor hashes; after bids close, a cipher-derived random sample of timestamps is checked against independent observations. Accounts whose reports trace to one sensor stream share one payout, regardless of names. A Sybil operator must deploy and maintain distinct sensors and bond each stream, while fabricated readings risk forfeiture. Shared public sensors can wrongly merge honest agents, so provenance disputes need an appeal path.
